title: Chicken and Mushroom Pie
subtitle: Tender chicken pieces in a creamy white-sauce filling under puff pastry
excerpt: Chicken and mushroom pie is a classic British pie: poached chicken and chestnut mushrooms in a creamy sauce, topped with a golden puff pastry lid. The filling is gentle rather than highly spiced, making this a reliable dish for any occasion. A good stock and a properly thickened sauce are what set it apart.
sourceNotes: A filling of chicken and mushrooms in a cream sauce under puff pastry has been a standard of British home cooking and catering since at least the mid-twentieth century.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze the cooked filling for up to 3 months. Defrost overnight, reheat until piping hot, top with fresh puff pastry, and bake.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Make the filling up to 2 days ahead and keep in the fridge. Top and bake on the day.

content.text: Chicken and mushroom pie uses poached chicken thighs and chestnut mushrooms in a cream sauce under a puff pastry lid. The thighs stay juicier than breast meat under long heat, and the mushrooms absorb the sauce and add a meaty depth. The sauce should be thick enough that a spoon drawn through it leaves a clear track.

Put {{chicken-thighs-boneless}} chicken thighs in a pan with {{stock-chicken}} of chicken stock and the thyme sprigs. Bring to a gentle simmer, cover, and poach for 18 to 20 minutes until cooked through. Lift out the chicken and set aside. Strain and reserve the stock.
When cool enough to handle, shred or cut the chicken into large pieces.

Melt {{unsalted-butter}} of butter in the same pan. Fry {{leek}} sliced leek until soft, 5 minutes. Add {{chestnut-mushrooms}} of mushrooms and cook until they release their liquid and it evaporates, about 6 minutes.

Stir in {{plain-flour}} of flour and cook for 1 minute. Gradually whisk in the reserved stock, then {{double-cream}} of double cream. Simmer until thick, about 5 minutes. Season well. Add the chicken pieces and stir to combine. Transfer to the pie dish and cool for 15 minutes.

Heat the oven to 200°C fan. Brush the rim of the dish with beaten egg. Lay the puff pastry over the filling, press down on the rim, and trim. Cut a small slit in the centre. Brush with beaten egg. Bake for 25 to 30 minutes until the pastry is puffed and deep golden.

items.symptom: The puff pastry is not rising
items.cause: The pastry was warm when it went into the oven, or the oven was not fully up to temperature.
items.fix: Keep the pastry chilled until the last moment. Put the pie straight into a fully preheated 200°C fan oven.

items.symptom: The sauce is thin after baking
items.cause: The filling had not cooled enough before baking, releasing steam that thinned the sauce.
items.fix: Cool the filling until no steam is rising before adding the pastry lid.

items.cause: It was overcooked during poaching or in the oven.
items.fix: Poach only until just cooked through. The chicken continues to cook inside the pie; it does not need to be done through twice.

items.symptom: The pastry is soggy in the middle
items.cause: Too much liquid in the filling, or the filling was not sealed under the pastry.
items.fix: Reduce the sauce until thick before filling. Make sure the steam vent is cut after laying the pastry, not before.

content.text: Chicken and mushroom pie sits alongside steak and kidney pie as one of the British pub kitchen's most reliable dishes. It is milder and lighter in flavour than the beef version, which gives it broader appeal. Served with a pile of greens and some roast potatoes, it is a complete and generous meal.
